Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failure occurs in the test `testToClass_object()`, which calls `ClassUtils.toClass(Object[])` with an array containing a null element. The current bug report states that `c0.m0(Object[])` (which corresponds to `ClassUtils.toClass(Object[])` based on the test context) throws a NullPointerException (NPE) when the array contains a null element.

Looking at the code for `ClassUtils.toClass(Object[])`, it first handles null and empty array cases correctly by returning null or an empty array. However, in the loop over the elements of the input array, it calls `array[i].getClass()` without null checking. If any element in the input array is null, calling `getClass()` on null will throw an NPE.

The test case specifically passes an array `new Object[] { "Test", null, 99d }`, which includes a null element. Since the code attempts to call `getClass()` on this null element at index 1, it results in the observed NullPointerException.

Therefore, the root cause is the missing null check in `ClassUtils.toClass(Object[])` when converting elements of the input array to their classes. It should handle null elements gracefully, likely by inserting null into the resulting Class<?> array at corresponding positions instead of throwing an exception.

The other provided recent bug reports are unrelated and do not mention similar problems with null handling or Class-related methods, so they offer no additional relevant insight.

In summary, the bug occurs because `ClassUtils.toClass(Object[])` assumes no null elements in the input array and does not check for null before calling `getClass()`. The test exposes this issue by passing a null element, triggering the NPE.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
